title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: Respondeo — παράπτωμα vs other names; deny major/minor
pass_a_gloss: I answer: split παράπτωμα from the other two. With that one name Paul sometimes marks Adam's sin, sometimes the vice born from it in all humans; with the other two he marks only Adam's sin—not actual sliced off from habitual, but actual-together-with-habitual. So for παράπτωμα I deny the major; for the other two, the minor.
pass_b_english: I answer that the name paraptoma must be distinguished from the other two: For by that one the Apostle sometimes designates Adam's sin, sometimes the vice arisen from Adam's sin in all humans: By these he signifies only Adam's sin, not indeed the actual cut off from the habitual, but together with the habitual. And so as far as this name paraptoma is concerned, I deny the Major: but as far as the other two, I deny the minor.
source_text: Respondeo distinguendum esse nomen παράπτωμα à duobus aliis: Illo enim Apostolus modo peccatum Adami, modo vitium ex peccato Adami in omnibus hominibus ortum designat: His solum peccatum Adami significat, non quidem actuale praecisum ab habituali, sed simul cum habituali. Itaque quantum ad hoc nomen παράπτωμα attinet, nego Maiorem: quantum vero ad alia duo, nego minorem.
